A_target.statement:
Let $t$ be a term of the untyped [[Definition:Lambda Calculus|$\lambda$-calculus]] which is typable in the [[Definition:Simply Typed Lambda Calculus|simply typed $\lambda$-calculus]] with type variables.
Then $t$ has a [[Definition:Principal Type|principal type]] $\sigma$, of which every type of $t$ is a substitution instance, and $\sigma$ is computable.

B_source.statement:
Let a finite set of equations between first-order terms be solvable.
Then it has a [[Definition:Most General Unifier|most general unifier]] $\theta$, computable by [[Robinson's Unification Algorithm]], and every solution factors as $\psi \circ \theta$.

substitutions.first-order terms: types built from type variables and arrows

object_map.reformulation: Reduce type inference to solving the equations that the typing rules impose on fresh type variables.

validity_conditions: Typability of t with type T is equivalent to solvability of the constraints together with tau_t = T.
The occurs check rules out untypable terms such as self-application.
proof_plan:
Give each variable and subterm of $t$ a fresh type variable.
For an application $u \, v$ add $\tau_u = \tau_v \to \alpha$ with $\alpha$ fresh; for an abstraction $\lambda x. u$ set its type to $\tau_x \to \tau_u$.
$t$ has type $T$ {{iff}} some substitution solves the constraints and sends $\tau_t$ to $T$.
By the source result, the constraints have a most general unifier $\theta$, and every solution is $\psi \circ \theta$.
